about: A small JavaScript library that reads English text and can change its tense, number and form.

prs.title: Common verbs get the right past tense
prs.broken: Verbs missing from the word list copied a look-alike irregular verb, so "budget" became "budgot" and "string" became "strought".
prs.changed: Seven verbs, including budget, string, summarise and panic, now have their correct forms listed.
prs.matters: Apps that rewrite text with this library no longer produce made-up words for everyday verbs.

prs.title: Plurals like toes and cheeses turn singular correctly
prs.broken: Making plurals singular cut some words short: "toes" became "to", "lies" became "ly" and "cheeses" became "chees".
prs.changed: Three new rules run first for these word shapes. Other words such as heroes and ladies come out as before.
prs.matters: Turning "toes" into "to" silently changes a sentence, so text rewritten by the library now stays correct.

prs.title: Last season now means the most recent one to end
prs.broken: In November, last summer pointed to the summer of the year before, even though this year's summer had already ended.
prs.changed: A year is now taken off only if the season has not ended yet, the same way last june already worked.
prs.matters: Apps that read dates from plain English get the season people mean.

prs.title: A clock before "tonight" means the evening
prs.broken: "7:45 tonight" came back as a quarter to eight in the morning, and "8 tonight" came back with no time at all.
prs.changed: A time written before tonight, this evening or tomorrow night is now read as an evening time.
prs.matters: "Meet me at 7:45 tonight" no longer lands twelve hours early.
